QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_16

answer.text: Slum area development and affordable housing
Bridging the digital divide in internet and mobile-phone access
Disaster management including relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction
Promoting gender equality, empowerment of women and LGBTQIA+ communities

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.5 maps SAS 400 to 'Promoting gender equality, empowerment of Women and LGBTQIA+ communities'. Slum/housing is SAS 1100; disaster management is SAS 1200; digital divide is SAS 1500. The Trap: SAS 1100 (A), SAS 1200 (C), and SAS 1500 (B) each have their own thematic area. SAS 400 is specifically gender. Cross-Exam Context: SAS numbering is XXIII-specific; candidates frequently confuse SAS 400 (gender) with SAS 1000 (livelihoods incl. women workers) — both touch women, but SAS 400 is the 'equality/empowerment' standard. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For SAS 400 (gender) engagements, sample both the direct beneficiary cohort and a control cohort from the same block — counterfactual is especially important because government schemes (PMMY, Ujjwala) often co-fund women-directed programs.
